data.title: Stephen Yiu explains why Nvidia stock isn't out of the woods just yet
data.description:
Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s (NVDA) chief executive was enough to put a potential lawsuit on hold for one shareholder. It hasn’t settled the questions that could still weigh on the stock.

Stephen Yiu, chief investment officer at Blue Whale Capital, told CNBC he was keeping his Nvidia stake unchanged while waiting to see what congressional questioning and ongoing investigations turn up.

His assessment comes as S&P Global Ratings put the chipmaker’s AA credit rating on “negative” watch, citing concerns about management and board oversight.

Huang’s return changed Yiu’s calculus on a lawsuit

“Probably not for the time being,” Yiu said when asked whether he was still considering legal action.

He had weighed that possibility if the leadership turmoil caused lasting damage to Nvidia’s share price. Huang’s quick return narrowed that window.

Nvidia announced Huang’s resignation on 12 November, before confirming on 23 November that its board had voted unanimously to reinstate him as chief executive, president and a director.

For shareholders, those 11 days mattered because they shortened the period in which Nvidia faced an open-ended search for a permanent successor.

The board’s independent investigation is continuing, however. Yiu said he would “sit tight” over the next couple of weeks as more information comes out. That leaves his response to any new disclosures open.

Strong sales give investors a reason to stay put

Yiu said Nvidia’s underlying business was “actually doing quite well” and suggested the share price might already reflect much of the bad news.

The latest earnings support his assessment. Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion on Nov. 17, up 103% from a year earlier.

The next risk for shareholders, in Yiu’s view, is another adverse disclosure that forces investors to revisit what they’ve already priced in.

S&P’s move puts that risk in focus. Nvidia retained its AA rating on Nov. 25, but the agency indicated it could lower the rating to AA− within 90 days if governance concerns persist.

Yiu called the decision “prudent.” For equity investors, the watch gives them a specific issue to follow alongside sales growth: how the board responds to questions about its oversight.

Congress could clarify how much risk sits with Nvidia

Yiu described Nvidia as “mission critical” to the US economy. For him, an unresolved question is whether any liability that emerges from the inquiries would fall on Huang personally or on Nvidia as a company.

The distinction matters to shareholders because findings about the company’s own controls could have implications for how Nvidia sells and distributes its chips.

House committee chairs have confirmed that Huang is due for a closed-door interview on Dec. 1 and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter is scheduled for Dec. 2.

Lawmakers are examining how advanced chips may have reached Chinese entities. Yiu said Blue Whale was keeping its position steady based on what it had learned so far.

The interviews could give investors a clearer basis for judging whether the scrutiny reaches Nvidia’s business practices.

data.title: SAP shares outlook as it plots another 10,000 round of layoffs: buy or sell?
data.description:
SAP share price has bounced back in the past four consecutive days as investors returned to software companies. It extended its gains, reaching its highest level since November 18, after reports of another round of layoffs emerged. It has jumped by 51% from its lowest level this year.

SAP to announce huge layoffs

SAP, one of the biggest enterprise software companies in the world, is planning to lay off thousands of employees in the coming months as the management works to boost its profitability.

According to the FT, the company plans to fire about 10,000 employees as it works to accelerate the use of AI in its business. It joins other similar companies that have announced substantial layoffs this year. 

Just recently, Microsoft announced a 60,000-person buyout, a move the management said was aimed at cutting costs. Other companies like Salesforce, Workday, and ServiceNow have announced layoffs this year. Similarly, in Germany, companies like BMW, Volkswagen, and BMW have announced layoffs this year.

This is not the first time that SAP has laid off workers. In 2024, management announced that they were laying off 10,000 in 2024, but the company made subsequent hirings that pushed its headcount to 113k.

READ MORE: SAP stock tumbles 3%: why Oracle's AI capex surge is hitting software shares

SAP’s business is growing 

The most recent results showed that SAP’s business continued growing as demand from enterprise companies rose. Its cloud backlog jumped by 28% to over €24 billion, with the cloud revenue and cloud ERP suite revenue rising by 26% and 29% to €6.6 billion and €5.96 billion, respectively.

SAP serves some of the biggest companies in the, including popular names like NTT, Toyota, Decathlon, AstraZeneca, and Henkel.

The upcoming layoffs come at a time when the company's profitability metrics have deteriorated in the past few quarters. It made a gross profit of 73.1% in the third quarter, down from 73.5% in the same period last year. Its profit after tax jumped to €2.26 billion.

Analysts are bullish on SAP shares

Top analysts are bullish on SAP shares, citing its revenue growth and growing backlog. JPMorgan upgraded the stock from neutral to overweight, while Erste Group boosted it from hold to buy. Other analysts who are bullish on the stock are from Barclays, Citigroup,and Goldman Sachs.

A key challenge, however, is that it is a highly overvalued company, with a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 27, much higher than the technology sector median of 18. Its forward price-to-earnings-to-growth (PEG) ratio has risen to 2.45, also higher than other companies. These multiples are much higher than those of other software companies like Microsoft, ServiceNow, and Workday.

SAP share price technical analysis

SAP stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that SAP stock has retreated sharply in the past few weeks. It has now plunged from a high of €220 in October to the current €194.15. 

The stock has dropped below the 23.6% Fibonacci Retracement level. It has also remained below the 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA).

The ongoing rebound is a sign that investors are buying the dip. However, there is a risk that this rebound is temporary. As such, there is a risk that it will drop further, potentially to the 50% retracement level of €173.

data.title: Shopify stock is still under pressure: Is it a buy as valuation concerns persist?
data.description:
Shopify stock price has plunged into a bear market, moving from the October high of $181 to the current $133. It has slumped below key moving averages, a trend that continued after releasing its earnings report,which showed that its revenue growth slowed during the quarter.

Shopify’s revenue growth is slowing 

SHOP stock has plunged into a bear market, moving from a high of $180 in October to the current $133. This retreat continued after the company published its financial results, which showed that its revenue growth was slowing.

Shopify said that its revenue rose to $3.7 billion in the third quarter from $2.8 billion in the same period last year. Most of this revenue was in its merchant solutions, with the rest being in its subscription solutions.

The company's net income jumped from $264 million in the third quarter of last year to $462 million. 

However, there are signs that other parts of the business are slowing, with its global merchandise volume remaining at 30% in the last three consecutive quarters. Its European GMV dropped from 42% in the second quarter of 2024 to 33%, with the North American figure remaining at 28%.

Analysts expect the company's revenue growth will remain under pressure in the coming quarters. The average estimate among analysts is that its fourth-quarter revenue is expected to come in at $4.6 billion, up by 31.1% from the same period last year.

If the estimate is correct, the annual revenue will come in at $15.3 billion, up by 32.50% from the same period last year. This growth will then slow to 26% next year to $19.3 billion, which is quite good for a company that has been in the business for two decades.

Shopify is benefiting from the market share of its business, since it is the biggest name in the e-commerce software industry. Most recently, there is hope that it will benefit from the rise of AI agents, which are now able to shop for people. As these agents become more popular, they will lead to more shopping activity over time.

READ MORE: Shopify stock has crossed a crucial resistance: will the rally persist?

Shopify valuation concerns remains 

The main challenge facing the SHOP stock is that its business has always been highly overvalued because of its growing market share, revenue and profitability growth, and its ability to continue monetizing its products.

Shopify has a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 70, and a forward PEG multiple of 2.19. In contrast, the S&P 500 Index has a multiple of 17, while the technology median is 18.2. These numbers are also higher than other companies, including retailers like Walmart and Costco.

The only valuation multiple that can justify Shopify’s current price is the Rule-of-40, which looks at a company’s revenue growth and its margins. By adding these two numbers, Shopify has a multiple of 47%, which is higher than the key level of 40.

Analysts have a bullish outlook for the stock. Argus reiterated the buy rating and set a target of $180, while Bernstein has a target of $165. Other analysts who are bullish on the company are from Needham, Wells Fargo, and UBS Group.

Shopify stock price technical analysis 

SHOP stock chart | Source: TradingView 

The daily chart shows that Shopify stock has dropped sharply since mid-October, moving from a high of $180 to the current $133.

Shopify has already dropped below the ascending trendline that connects the lowest swings since May 14 this year.

The stock has also dropped below the 50-day and 200-day moving averages and is now hovering between the 50% and 61.8% Fibonacci retracement level.

Therefore, the stock will likely remain under pressure for a while and possibly retest the support at $100 and then bounce back, possibly to $150 in the future.

data.title: Air Canada stock is facing turbulence: Will the falling jet fuel prices rescue it?
data.description:
Air Canada stock is facing turbulence as jet fuel prices remain elevated, which is hurting its profit metrics. AC dropped to $22 on Thursday, down by about 30% from its highest point this year. Still, on the positive side, there is a possibility that the company will benefit once the US-Iran war ends, which will happen possibly in the first quarter of next year.

Jet fuel prices may drop after the US-Iran war ends

Air Canada and other airlines have suffered substantially because of the rising jet fuel prices. IATA data shows that jet fuel prices have soared by over 71% from the same period last year. 

On the positive side, there are signs that the trend is changing as crude oil prices remain under pressure. Brent and the West Texas Intermediate (WTI) has dropped by over 20% from the October high. 

According to IATA, the average jet fuel price has dropped to $154.7 per barrel, down by 20% from the previous month. This drop has happened across all regions, especially in Europe and North America.

There is a likelihood that this trend will continue in the coming months as odds that the US and Iran war will end rise. In a statement to the New York Post, President Donald Trump said that he may resume the bombing campaign in January. 

He also said that he has the funds to last the war through January. As such, there is a possibility that he wants the Democrats to remove the funding and blame them for losing the war. Trump believes that he has no good options left since Iran is playing the hard ball in terms of negotiations. Iran has also warned that it will retaliate if the US launches its attacks.

Therefore, there is a likelihood that crude oil prices will drop further in the coming months. If this happens, jet fuel prices will likely continue falling in the near term, helping Air Canada boost its earnings. 

Air Canada’s business is growing, but risks remain

Air Canada shares have plunged in the past few months as the cost of doing business rose. Its last earnings showed that the company transported 13.3 million passengers, up by 9.6% from a year earlier. It also benefited from hiking fares to cover the rising costs. 

Air Canada’s revenue jumped by 21% to $7 billion, while its operational costs jumped by 22% to $6.7 billion. The company’s chief executive officer (CEO) said:

“Decisive pricing, capacity and cost actions helped mitigate the impact of a $906 million year-over-year increase in fuel expense, with fuel prices 10 cents per litre above our third quarter expectations.”

Still, the company lowered its forward guidance. It now expects that its adjusted EBITDA will be between $2.4 billion and $2.7 billion, down from the previous guidance of between $2.9 billion and $3.2 billion. These fundamentals will likely improve as the cost of jet fuel increases.

Air Canada stock price technical analysis

AC stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the AC stock has remained under pressure in the past few months. It has slumped from a high of $31.46 in August to the current $22. 

The stock has remained above the ascending trendline that connects the lowest swings in April last year, March, and October this year. Moving below that trendline is a sign that the uptrend remains intact.

Therefore, there is a likelihood that the stock will bounce back in the coming months. If this happens, the next important level to watch will be at $25. A drop below that line will point to more downside over time.

data.title: Why is Meta facing protests and legal challenges in India?
data.description:
For years, Mark Zuckerberg was synonymous with a grey crewneck T-shirt. He has since moved towards a more unconventional wardrobe, but in India, his latest makeover on street posters has taken on a vastly different meaning.

Posters across India's technology capital, Bengaluru, depicted Zuckerberg wearing a white shirt, khaki shorts and a black cap.

The outfit resembles the traditional uniform of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), a Hindu nationalist organisation that serves as the ideological parent of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

These posters, which also showed the Meta founder performing the RSS salute, were put up by the youth wing of India's main opposition Congress party.

Zuckerberg is referred to as "BJPberg" in the posters and also termed "the son of BJP."

Congress has accused the social media giant of favouring Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and it has been targeting Meta.

Tensions between Meta and Congress have been simmering for more than a week, with youth workers protesting outside the company's offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram. Demonstrations have also spread to Bengaluru, Delhi and other cities.

The dispute has now reached the courts, with Congress on Wednesday filing a petition against Meta and the Indian government over what it describes as systematic censorship of opposition voices on Facebook and Instagram.

Why is Congress protesting against Meta?

The immediate trigger was the restriction of Instagram accounts belonging to two senior Indian Youth Congress officials, including its national president Uday Bhanu Chib.

The party alleges that Meta has been removing or restricting posts critical of Modi and the BJP while allowing content favourable to the ruling party to remain accessible.

Congress also claims the platform's automated moderation system has been targeting posts containing the name or photographs of Rahul Gandhi, the leader of the opposition in India's parliament.

In its petition before the Delhi High Court, the party cited examples of seemingly harmless content being restricted, including birthday greetings, tributes and even a wedding invitation featuring Gandhi.

One example involved a birthday greeting posted on November 8 by a Youth Congress leader. The post showed the leader standing alongside Gandhi but was blocked on the same day.

Congress argues that these restrictions go beyond what the government actually ordered Meta to remove and have created an uneven playing field ahead of several crucial state elections scheduled for early 2027.

The party has asked the court to overturn the automated takedown mandate, restore the restricted posts and require Meta to disclose how its blocking system works.

Why is Meta blocking so much content in India?

The controversy is closely connected to amendments made by the Indian government to its Information Technology rules in February 2026.

Previously, major social media platforms were asked to make efforts to use automated tools to identify duplicate copies of content that had already been taken down following government or court orders.

The February amendments made the requirement mandatory.

Large platforms must now deploy appropriate technical measures, including automated tools, to proactively identify and restrict content that is identical to material previously flagged for removal.

The rules also require platforms to take down unlawful content within three hours of receiving a valid government or court order, compared with the earlier 36-hour deadline.

For Meta, this has created a substantial compliance challenge. Facebook and Instagram have hundreds of millions of users in India, making the country its biggest market by users.

Failing to comply with Indian regulations could expose the company to legal consequences and jeopardise the legal protections available to online intermediaries.

Meta says it is restricting identical copies of previously removed material at scale and within India to comply with the amended rules.

The company has also acknowledged that it is still testing and refining its automated systems because of the unprecedented nature of the requirements.

Its latest transparency disclosures, accessed by Reuters, show that Meta restricted more than 5.4 million items in India during the first half of 2026 under local laws, compared with approximately 70,000 during the whole of 2025.

The sharp increase is largely connected to new rules.

Congress argues that Meta's actions are at the behest of the ruling party as similar posts uploaded by BJP's accounts have not been taken down.

However, Meta has said that it remains neutral towards ⁠all political parties.

The company's top executives in India held closed-door talks with the ‌Congress party on Tuesday but did not make any commitments. Congress now has taken Meta to court.

The ruling BJP, meanwhile, has criticised the protests.

National spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused Congress workers of vandalising Meta's Hyderabad office, describing the incident as an example of the party's approach towards private businesses.

data.title: Samsung, SK Hynix stocks surge: why smart money sees a buying opportunity
data.description:
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix stocks rallied on Friday as bargain hunters returned to South Korean semiconductor stocks following a turbulent week of trading.

Samsung rose 3.91% and SK Hynix gained 4.08%, helping lift the benchmark KOSPI by 3.52%.

The recovery comes as some global fund managers increase their exposure to the chipmakers, despite lingering concerns about memory oversupply and the sustainability of artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.

Samsung, SK Hynix shares: Institutional investors return to battered chip stocks

Jupiter Asset Management has modestly increased its holdings in both companies this week, even as uncertainty surrounding the broader technology sector persists.

“Valuations do look extremely cheap in some of our tech stocks,” Sam Konrad, an Asian equities investment manager at Jupiter, told the Financial Times.

The fund manager also identified signs of market capitulation.

Both chipmakers have lost more than half their value from their recent peaks, leaving investors questioning whether the sell-off has gone too far.

Meanwhile, foreign investors had bought a net 852.3 billion won of KOSPI shares by early afternoon, while individual investors were net sellers of 1.12 trillion won.

SK Hynix was also the most heavily net-bought stock among Mirae Asset Securities clients whose investment returns ranked in the top 1% over the preceding month, the Seoul Economic Daily reported.

Are Samsung and SK Hynix stocks too cheap to ignore?

The scale of the correction looks particularly striking when measured against the chipmakers' recent financial performance.

Samsung reported third-quarter operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, while SK Hynix earned 83.33 trillion won in operating profit on revenue of 104.62 trillion won.

At Wednesday's closing prices, Samsung and SK Hynix traded at just 2.29 and 2.01 times projected 2027 earnings.

Even if earnings were half those estimates, both stocks would have traded at less than five times those hypothetical profits.

Daol Investment & Securities analysts Nam Dae-jong and Kim Yeon-mi described the correction as “excessively steep relative to fundamentals”, according to The Herald Business.

The brokerage values Samsung at 300,000 won and SK Hynix at 2 million won.

However, those valuations depend on future profitability. A prolonged memory glut could undermine the earnings estimates that make both companies appear so inexpensive today.

AI demand and shareholder returns could sustain recovery

Long-term customer agreements may offer some protection against the volatility that has historically characterised the memory industry.

SK Hynix has secured agreements covering more than half its production capacity for 2027 and 2028. It also expects HBM4 to become its mainstream high-bandwidth memory product this quarter.

Shareholder distributions offer another potential catalyst. Samsung expects returns of up to 110 trillion won this year, while SK Hynix plans approximately 100 trillion won.

“Between Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, we favor SK hynix, which has already moved ahead with shareholder returns,” Hanwha Investment & Securities strategist Ha Jang-kwon said, according to Korea JoongAng Daily.

Samsung is expected to announce further details of its shareholder-return plans in January.

Nevertheless, rising manufacturing capacity, higher borrowing costs and uncertainty surrounding AI investment could continue to weigh on both stocks.

data.title: Enbridge stock could be at risk of falling to $61.5 despite strong revenue growth
data.description:
Enbridge stock has slumped in the second half of the year, even as the company’s business has continued doing well. ENB was trading at $66.50 in Canada, down sharply from the year-to-date high of $80.6, and technicals suggest that the company has more downside. 

Enbridge stock has fallen as its revenue has continued growing

ENB stock has dropped substantially, even as its business has continued doing well. This decline has coincided with that of other companies in the oil and gas transport industry. 

Energy Transfer, the biggest player in the United States, has tumbled by over 14% from the year-to-date high. Enterprise Products Partners (EPD) has fallen by 10.4%, while Kinder Morgan, Western Midstream, and Williams have fallen by double digits.

The ongoing retreat has also coincided with the stock market weakness, with the TSX Composite and S&P 500 being in a correction. The Nasdaq 100 Index has dropped into a bear market. 

Enbridge stock has also dropped because of property outages. Earlier this month, the company was forced to shut its North Dakota pipeline because of contamination concerns. Also, the company diluted its shareholders by raising C$3 billion in September to fund its acquisitions.

The most recent results showed that Enbridge’s revenue rose to $21 billion in the three months to September from $14.6 billion in the same period last year. This revenue brought its nine-month figure to $72.7 billion from $48 billion last year. 

The company’s growth was driven by the rising volumes of natural gas and crude oil. Its commodity sales business brought in over $14.8 billion in revenue, up from $8.3 billion in the same period last year. In contrast, its gas distribution and transportation businesses experienced modest growth.

Enbridge’s profits continued rising, with the earnings rising to $1.44 billion, up sharply from $847 million in the same period last year. Earnings in the first nine months of the year jumped to over $4.7 billion.

Enbridge’s management is also betting on growth through acquisitions. It recently announced a $2.5 billion buyout of Tallgrass Energy’s crude oil transportation, gathering, storage, and terminaling assets in a $2.5 billion deal. The deal provided it with a strategic connection between Bakken, Powder River Basin, and Denver-Julesburg basins. 

Analysts are upbeat about Enbridge’s stock. Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) reiterated its outperform rating, while TD Securities maintained its buy rating. Goldman Sachs’s John Mackay has a neutral outlook with a target of $50 for its US shares. 

Enbridge share price technical analysis

ENB stock chart | Source: TradingView

On the weekly chart, we see that the ENB stock has been under pressure in the second half of the year. It has now dropped below the 50-week exponential moving average (EMA). 

The stock has settled along the 38.2% Fibonacci Retracement level. This retracement is drawn by connecting the lowest level in 2023 and the all-time high of $80.

The stock has formed a bearish flag pattern, which is made up of a vertical line and a horizontal channel. This pattern tends to a continuation. Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling, potentially to the 50% retracement level of $61.50.

data.title: These 3 retail stocks are best positioned to benefit from Thanksgiving in 2026
data.description:
The Thanksgiving shopping rush looks a little smaller this year.

The National Retail Federation estimates 182.7 million consumers plan to shop between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday, down from 186.9 million last year.

Black Friday alone is expected to draw 126 million shoppers.

With more consumers starting early, the retailers best positioned to benefit are the ones giving shoppers several reasons to spend across the weekend.

Walmart can turn a grocery trip into a gift purchase, Target is using exclusives to bring people into stores, and Amazon is putting deals inside a football broadcast.

Walmart can turn a $35 dinner into a bigger shopping basket

Walmart (WMT) advertised a 26-item Thanksgiving meal basket for $35 that serves 10. At $3.5 a person, the offer gives households a concrete reason to choose it for one of November’s biggest grocery trips.

The payoff can come from what shoppers add to the order, from roasting pans and extra desserts to toys they were already planning to buy.

Walmart’s main Black Friday sale went online Nov. 23, overlapping with the final days of Thanksgiving prep.

In-store deals begin Friday morning. That timing matters because Walmart’s US e-commerce sales rose 23% in its latest quarter.

A customer who orders groceries online can browse holiday deals in the same place, giving Walmart another chance to win the gift purchase before that shopper opens a rival’s app.

Target gives Black Friday shoppers a reason to show up

Target (TGT) has $30 Thanksgiving meal for six but the bigger opportunity comes Friday morning. The first 100 eligible shoppers at each store get a gift card, with one card per location worth $1,000.

Target is also rolling out exclusive Pokémon and Topps trading-card products. A giveaway can get people through the door. An exclusive gives them something to buy that they can’t easily price-check at a rival.

Target enters the weekend with store comparable sales up 4.6% in its latest quarter.

The question for investors is how much of that traffic turns into a fuller cart. A shopper who comes for a collectible and leaves with holiday décor, wrapping paper or another gift makes the promotion more valuable than the giveaway alone would suggest.

Amazon brings the sale to the football audience

Amazon’s (AMZN) holiday sale runs through Nov. 30, with two rounds of featured deals on both Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

Its most distinctive sales pitch comes during Friday’s Pittsburgh Steelers–Denver Broncos game on Prime Video.

Viewers can use their remote or the Amazon Shopping app to see featured deals and buy merchandise during the broadcast, giving Amazon a chance to reach people who tuned in for football and may never have planned to browse a sale.

That extra attention has value beyond the items Amazon sells directly. Independent merchants can pay Amazon for services such as fulfillment, and brands can pay for ad placements.

For investors, that means a busy shopping weekend can generate revenue for Amazon even when another merchant makes the sale.

data.title: Fed rate hike odds rise to almost 100%: can AI selloff force a rethink?
data.description:
Markets are pricing in a near-certain probability of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates for the second time in three months at its December meeting.

CME FedWatch data on Thursday showed a 99.4% probability of a rate hike in December, which would take the federal funds rate to the 4%-4.25% range. The implied probability was around 97% a day earlier.

Wednesday's inflation data appears to have essentially confirmed the expectations of another increase after the Kevin Warsh-led committee raised rates in September for the first time in three years.

The latest figures have also raised questions about how much further borrowing costs may need to rise in 2027.

However, the prospect of additional tightening comes at a difficult time for financial markets.

A sharp selloff in artificial intelligence stocks has rattled Wall Street, with the Nasdaq 100 briefly entering bear-market territory on Wednesday, November 25, before recovering from its session lows.

This has raised a difficult question for policymakers: could the deterioration in financial markets force the Fed to reconsider its tightening plans?

Inflation data strengthen case for a hike

The US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, rose 3.8% year over year in October, according to data released by the Commerce Department on Wednesday.

Core PCE inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, increased to 3.3%, exceeding economists' expectations by 0.1 percentage point.

Both measures remain considerably above the Fed's 2% inflation target, suggesting that price pressures have yet to return to levels policymakers consider acceptable.

The latest figures followed October's consumer price index report, which showed headline inflation rising 0.4% on a monthly basis, compared with expectations of 0.3%. Core CPI increased 0.3%, matching the previous two months but exceeding the 0.2% forecast.

Meanwhile, the US economy expanded at an annualised rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, according to the revised Commerce Department estimate.

That was 0.9 percentage point higher than the initial estimate, reflecting stronger investment and consumer spending.

The combination of persistent inflation and resilient economic growth gives policymakers little immediate reason to abandon their tightening approach.

Williams reinforces Fed's inflation priority

New York Fed President John Williams has also stressed that bringing inflation back to the central bank's target remains essential.

Speaking at the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York on November 23, Williams said inflation remained too high and that policymakers still had work to do.

"But getting inflation back to 2% is 100% essential," he said.

He also acknowledged that monetary policy cannot resolve supply-side disruptions directly, including problems affecting shipping routes, pipelines and refineries.

However, he argued that the Fed must prevent such shocks from creating persistent inflationary pressures or weakening inflation expectations.

Other Fed policymakers have also maintained similar views, suggesting that they are unlikely to tolerate elevated inflation simply because financial markets are struggling.

Can AI selloff force Fed to reconsider?

The growing turmoil in technology stocks has nevertheless introduced another consideration into the rate debate.

The Nasdaq 100 briefly fell 20% below its October peak on Wednesday, meeting the definition of a bear market before recovering from its lows.

Investors have been reducing exposure to AI-linked companies amid concerns about enormous infrastructure spending, expensive financing and uncertainty over whether the investments will generate sufficient returns.

The Nvidia-Jensen Huang scandal regarding a suspected Chinese spy has also worried investors as the chipmaker and its star CEO remain central to the AI trade.

Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo Global Management, believes the market turmoil provides a strong argument for caution.

"If they look at inflation, they should be hiking. But if you look at the outlook for AI, they should maybe be cutting," Slok told the Financial Times.

He described the recent market turmoil as a very strong argument against aggressive rate increases.

Claudia Sahm, chief economist at New Century Advisors, was less convinced that the selloff would change the Fed's immediate direction.

"At this point, it's going to be hard to get them off this focus on inflation," she said to the Financial Times, adding that stock declines would need to become considerably larger to influence policymakers.

A decline in equity prices can tighten financial conditions by making it more expensive for companies to raise capital and reducing household wealth.

Bill Ackman warns against another rate hike

Pershing Square founder Bill Ackman has been among the most vocal critics of the Fed's tightening approach.

In a post on X, Ackman argued that financial conditions had already tightened substantially, pointing to rising borrowing costs and the recent decline in stock prices.

He also questioned the central bank's 2% inflation target, arguing that geopolitical risks, tariffs, military expenditure and massive investments in AI infrastructure and energy have fundamentally changed the economic environment.

Ackman believes a 3% inflation target would be more realistic under current circumstances.

"The Fed will put the U.S. and world in recession if it continues to raise rates in a failed attempt to drive inflation to 2%," he warned.

For now, however, markets are overwhelmingly positioned for another increase.

The December 8-9 meeting will test whether policymakers remain focused on persistent inflation or become concerned about the economic consequences of tighter financial conditions.

data.title: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) forecast ahead of earnings: will it rebound or fall?
data.description:
Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) stock has dropped into a correction, moving from a record high of $306 in July to $269 today. This retreat has coincided with the ongoing weakness of Canadian and US banks. Focus now shifts to its earnings, which will come out on December 3.

RBC Bank is falling as global banks drop

Royal Bank of Canada, the biggest bank in Canada, is a top player that offers diverse services, including personal banking, commercial banking, wealth management, insurance, and capital markets. It has the biggest market share in the country, which helps it generate over $66 billion a year.

RBC stock has dropped recently because of the ongoing weakness in the banking industry. A closer look at most banks stocks shows that many of them have pulled back in the past few months. 

The most recent results showed that RBC’s business did well in the second quarter, with its revenue rising by 11% to $18.3 billion. The closely-watched net income rose to $6 billion, while the return on equity rose to 17.9%.

READ MORE: Royal Bank of Canada stock double-tops ahead of Q1 earnings

Most of its businesses did well during the quarter. For example, its wealth management division grew by 32% to $1.44 billion, helped by its higher fee-based assets. Its commercial banking revenue rose by 12% to $936 million, while its capital markets segment made $1.54 billion, up by 16% from a year earlier. 

These segments helped to offset the decline in its insurance and personal computing business. 

RBC to publish earnings next week

Therefore, looking ahead, the upcoming earnings report is expected to show that its business continued growing, driven by its wealth management division. 

The challenge, however, is that its capital markets business likely remained under pressure in the fourth fiscal quarter. This business has been relatively weak because of the rising interest rates. Indeed, a report by the London Stock Exchange showed that global deal value dropped by 41% in the third quarter to $993 billion. 

Most companies also published slower investment banking revenue. Morgan Stanley’s investment banking revenue rose by 2% to $2.16 billion, while Citigroup’s, JPMorgan, and Goldman Sachs grew by 9%, 15%, and 21%, respectively. 

Yahoo Finance data shows that analysts expect the upcoming earnings to show that its revenue rose by 7.37% to $18.48 billion. The earnings per share is expected to move to $4.15 from $3.85 in the same period last year. Investors will focus on its net income margin and its wealth management and investment banking business. Also, markets will react to its costs, which have been rising recently. Its non-interest expense rose by 6% in the third quarter.

Analysts have a muted outlook for the company. Scotiabank reiterated its outperform rating, while Barclays maintained its overweight position. TD Securities also maintained a buy rating, while Raymond James downgraded its rating from outperform to market outperform. The average target among analysts on its US shares is $227, up by 20% from the current level. 

RBC stock price technical analysis

RBC stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the Royal Bank of Canada share price has been under pressure in the past few months. It dropped from $306 in June to the current $268. 

The stock has now settled along the 23.6% Fibonacci Retracement level, which also coincides with the lowest level on October 8. It has dropped below the 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) and the Supertrend indicator.

The stock has already invalidated the double-bottom pattern at $268. Therefore, there is a risk that it continues falling, potentially to the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level at $247, which is about 8.2% below the current level.
